checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does P256VERIFY precompile correctly trigger out-of-gas revert when available_gas < 6900?

reachability.notes: A caller can deliberately provide exactly 6899 gas to trigger the out-of-gas revert. The behavior must be consistent with standard EVM out-of-gas handling.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Deploy a contract that calls P256VERIFY with controlled gas stipend. 2. Call P256VERIFY with exactly 6899 gas and verify out-of-gas revert occurs. 3. Verify all remaining gas is consumed (standard EVM OOG semantics). 4. Test boundary cases: 6898, 6899, 6900, 6901 gas. 5. Compare behavior across multiple client implementations. 6. Check that no partial execution state leaks on OOG.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0058, Pre-condition: EIP7951-SG006-INV-002, Trust Boundary: tb-002

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does get_blob_parameters use descending (reverse) epoch sort for BLOB_SCHEDULE lookup?

reachability.notes: Sorting direction is critical for correct schedule lookup. Descending sort finds the most recent applicable entry. Ascending sort would find the earliest entry, returning outdated parameters.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Create a BLOB_SCHEDULE with multiple entries at different epochs (e.g., epoch 10, 20, 30 with different max_blobs). 2. Query get_blob_parameters for epoch 25. 3. Verify it returns parameters from epoch 20 (most recent applicable), NOT epoch 10 (earliest). 4. Test edge cases: exact epoch match, epoch before all entries, epoch after all entries. 5. Compare results across all client implementations. 6. Verify sorting is stable and deterministic.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is compute_fork_digest hashing scheme identical across all clients (encoding, concatenation order, hash function)?

reachability.notes: Any deviation in byte encoding (e.g., uint64 vs uint256, big-endian vs little-endian) or concatenation order (epoch+max_blobs vs max_blobs+epoch) would produce different hashes, causing network partitions.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Create test vectors with known blob_parameters (epoch, max_blobs_per_block). 2. Compute fork_digest using uint_to_bytes(epoch) + uint_to_bytes(max_blobs_per_block). 3. Verify exact byte representation: check endianness (little-endian per SSZ), byte width (uint64), zero-padding. 4. Compare hash outputs across all client implementations (Lighthouse, Prysm, Teku, Nimbus, Lodestar). 5. Test edge cases: epoch=0, max_blobs=0, maximum values. 6. Verify concatenation order is epoch-first in all implementations.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0060, Assumption: asm-010, Trust Boundary: tb-010

checklist.title: Is the fork upgrade to Fulu irreversible - can any state transition revert fork.current_version to a pre-Fulu version?

reachability.notes: Fork irreversibility is consensus-critical. A reversible fork would allow fork oscillation attacks.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Apply upgrade_to_fulu(state) and capture post-state. 2. Verify post.fork.current_version == FULU_FORK_VERSION. 3. Enumerate all state transition functions and verify none can modify fork.current_version. 4. Test reorg scenarios: can a chain reorg crossing the fork boundary cause oscillation? 5. Verify state serialization/deserialization preserves fork version. 6. Check for any code paths that could write to fork.current_version after upgrade.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0003, Invariant: fork-SG-001-INV-003, Trust Boundary: tb-007

checklist.title: Does upgrade_to_fulu preserve all state fields except fork and proposer_lookahead?

reachability.notes: State preservation during fork is consensus-critical. Triggered automatically at fork epoch via P2P consensus.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Create a comprehensive pre-state with non-default values for all electra.BeaconState fields. 2. Apply upgrade_to_fulu(pre_state) to get post_state. 3. For each field F in pre_state (except fork, proposer_lookahead): assert post_state.F == pre_state.F. 4. Test with edge-case field values: empty lists, maximum size lists, boundary values. 5. Verify validators list is fully preserved (balances, pubkeys, withdrawal credentials). 6. Check for any implicit field zeroing or truncation during type conversion.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0004, Invariant: fork-SG-002-INV-001, Assumption: asm-009

checklist.title: After upgrade_to_fulu, is post.fork.previous_version == pre.fork.current_version (fork version chain maintained)?

reachability.notes: Incorrect version chaining would cause P2P fork digest mismatches.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Create pre_state with fork.current_version = ELECTRA_FORK_VERSION. 2. Apply upgrade_to_fulu(pre_state) to get post_state. 3. Assert post_state.fork.previous_version == ELECTRA_FORK_VERSION. 4. Assert post_state.fork.current_version == FULU_FORK_VERSION. 5. Verify fork.epoch is set correctly to FULU_FORK_EPOCH. 6. Compute fork digest from post_state and verify it matches expected value for Fulu fork.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0005, Invariant: fork-SG-002-INV-002, Assumption: asm-009
